title: Resolution strategy for model selection in SDK: tag/semver/commit precedence
creator: Evelyn Carter
description: Define explicit, deterministic semantics for model version pin resolution in Redwood SDKs and API so that developers can reliably pin by tag, semver, semver range, or commit hash while preserving performance-profile stability and clear fallback behavior.
problem_statement: Customers need predictable programmatic control over which model binary and performance profile is used for inference. Existing behavior is underspecified in edge cases (mixed tags vs semver ranges, ambiguous tags, absent performance profiles) which causes silent regressions and surprising fallbacks under capacity pressure.
proposal_summary: Introduce a single resolution algorithm that is implemented identically in the server-side resolver and SDK clients: a priority-ordered matching chain (explicit-ref > exact-semver > semver-range > annotated-tag > channel alias > latest-stable). Publish performance-profile bindings as immutable metadata on model versions; when a pin resolves to a version without a published profile for the requested workload, surface a validation warning and apply a documented fallback policy rather than silently using an incompatible profile.
resolution_rules: 1) If request supplies an explicit commit/ref (40+ hex or provider commit), resolve to that exact build; fail if not found (error PIN-RES-001).
2) Else if request supplies exact semver (e.g., 2.3.1), resolve to matching release with highest patch in that release line; fail if absent (error PIN-RES-002).

3) Else if request supplies semver range (e.g., ^2.3 || >=2.5 <3.0), resolve to highest compatible version with published profile for the requested workload; if multiple candidates, prefer the one with strongest performance-match score.

4) Else if request supplies a tag (user-defined label), resolve to the version the tag currently points to, but include tag-metadata in response. If tag is ambiguous (multiple model families), return 409 with explanatory payload (error PIN-RES-007).
5) Channel aliases (stable, staging, nightly) are syntactic sugar for predefined semver ranges and are resolved server-side per-customer config.

6) If resolution succeeds but the resolved version lacks a performance profile for the request's target workload or hardware class, return a resolvable warning (code PIN-PROF-001) and use the fallback profile selection rules: exact-architecture match > closest-quantization-profile > best latency-estimate. Documented numeric priority applied.

7) In capacity-constrained or compatibility-failover cases, the routing layer may substitute a lower-cost compatible variant only when the request explicitly allows fallback (flag allowFallback=true). Such substitution is audited in the response and console traces.
8) All resolution decisions return deterministic metadata in the operation response: resolved_version, resolved_profile_id, resolution_path, and decision_reasons (strings).
api_contract_examples: SDK example (python): client.generate(model='acme-llama@commit:3a4f2c', allow_fallback=False) -> raises ModelResolutionError(PIN-RES-001) if commit missing
Tag example: model='translation-ru:tag:prod-v2' will return resolved_version and tag metadata; ambiguous tag -> 409 response
Semver range example: model='acme-llama@^2.1.0' chooses highest matching build with a performance profile for the runtime hardware.
sdk_changelog_notes: Add ModelResolutionError and structured ResolutionResult to SDKs; include resolved_version, resolved_profile, and resolution_path in successful responses.
New client option: allow_fallback (default true) and strict_resolution (default false) to toggle runtime fallback behavior.
Deprecate implicit 'latest' resolution without namespace in next major SDK release; warn when used.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover commit, exact semver, semver range, tag, and channel alias resolution paths.
Integration tests simulate missing performance profile and assert warning code PIN-PROF-001 and documented fallback chosen.
SDK surface exposes ResolutionResult with deterministic fields in Python, TS/JS, and Go clients.
Server resolver and SDKs return identical resolution_path strings for canonical inputs (golden fixtures).
Backward compatibility tests: existing requests without explicit pins continue to resolve to previous behavior with deprecation warnings logged.
implementation_notes: Server: implement resolver with modular matcher chain and pluggable scoring function used by semver-range selection. SDKs: add synchronous resolution check in client before enqueueing request to surface early errors. Performance-profile registry exposes immutable profile ids that are returned alongside version metadata. Audit logs record original pin, resolved_version, resolved_profile_id, and allow_fallback flag.
testing_plan: Create a resolution test matrix documenting 36 combinations of input type (commit/semver/range/tag/alias) x profile availability x allowFallback flag.
Add end-to-end canary in staging that exercises rollback scenario where a new profile is missing and ensure the resolver emits PIN-PROF-001 and that SDK strict_resolution prevents silent fallbacks.
Load test: validate resolver throughput under 50k req/s and measure added latency (target +1ms p50).
risks: Changing default fallback semantics could break customers who implicitly relied on silent substitutions; mitigated by deprecation warnings and default allow_fallback=true for one release cycle.

Semver-range scoring ambiguity across model families could lead to non-deterministic selection if metadata not normalized; require canonical publishing pipeline to populate quality_score and hardware_compat tags.
SDKs adding pre-resolution increases client-side complexity and may surface transient network errors earlier; fall back to server-side validation when network unavailable.
rollback_plan: If we observe >0.5% increase in customer errors referencing PIN-RES-* within 24 hours of release, revert SDK change that enables strict pre-resolution and flip a server-side feature flag to restore previous resolution flow while we patch semantics.
monitoring_and_alerting: Instrument metrics: resolution.success_rate, resolution.latency_ms_p50/95/99, resolution.warn_count(PIN-PROF-001), resolution.error_count(PIN-RES-*)
Create alert: resolution.error_rate > 0.1% sustained for 10m -> P0 oncall
Add dashboard: top unresolved tags, most frequent semver-range hits, and distribution of resolution_path types.
rollout_strategy: Server resolver: rollout via feature flag to 10% of traffic for 48h, increase to 50% for 24h, then GA. SDKs: ship opt-in beta in minor release, then default in next minor with deprecation warnings for older clients.
